question: Should the shared `agent-transcript` skill automatically discover GitHub Copilot local sessions and make their allowlisted dialogue eligible for public PR or issue provenance?
rationale: This is a new local-data collection and disclosure boundary, so code review alone cannot establish the repository's intended privacy policy or consent model.

options.title: Approve a narrow Copilot source
options.body: Approve the feature only after final-head redacted proof confirms that Copilot discovery is local-only and all non-dialogue or sensitive content fails closed.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in
options.body: Keep Copilot parsing available but require an explicit command-line source selection before any Copilot session is discovered or rendered.

options.title: Defer the source
options.body: Do not add Copilot discovery to the shared skill until maintainers define a broader local-session privacy policy.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow Copilot source
recommendation.body: Approve the feature only after final-head redacted proof confirms that Copilot discovery is local-only and all non-dialogue or sensitive content fails closed.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository-level follow-up owner is the best available low-confidence routing fallback for a shared-skill privacy-boundary decision.
